name: fail-anchor-proof-graft
note: a packed anchor whose cosig cannot reach the anchor's signed head — a claimed anchor is either verifiable or a lie; every verifier fails closed

name: fail-bool-leaf-index
note: leaf_index true — bool is an int subclass in Python but not an integer in JSON; Number.isInteger parity rejects it

name: fail-doctored-verifier
note: a post-export edit to verify_case.py — membership checks names, only the signed pin checks the bytes

name: fail-embedded-foreign-receipt
note: an embedded receipt signed outside the issuer lineage — embedded evidence must bind the pack's issuer or it is grafted testimony

name: fail-embedded-tampered-receipt
note: an embedded receipt's payload flipped — payload hash and signature both fail; a doctored observation can never ride the signed head

name: fail-foreign-pin
note: a valid pin receipt under an untrusted key — signature integrity is not issuer authority

name: fail-forged-verifier-tool
note: a modified verify_bundle.py fails its own signed pin — membership whitelists names, only the manifest pins bytes

name: fail-fractional-leaf-index
note: leaf_index 5.5 — non-integral indices are not integers on any surface; Python must not silently truncate where JS rejects

name: fail-grafted-log-proof
note: another receipt's audit path grafted on — the Merkle math catches what a presence check never would

name: fail-grafted-pin
note: a verifier_manifest signed for another pack cannot pin this one — the scope binding stops the replay

name: fail-media-mismatch
note: media bytes that don't hash to the signed digest are caught

name: fail-missing-listed
note: a bundle the signed manifest lists but the zip lacks fails

name: fail-missing-log-proof
note: a pack receipt silently dropped from log_checkpoint.json — the pack cannot claim log membership it does not prove

name: fail-missing-pinned-tool
note: a tool the signed pin names but the pack lacks fails — the pin binds both directions

name: fail-orphan-rotation
note: a rotation the successor never countersigned cannot pivot trust

name: fail-oversize-tree-size
note: a properly SIGNED head claiming tree_size 2^40 — valid signature, impossible size: JS bitwise ops die past 2^31, so every surface rejects it rather than diverging

name: fail-payload-tamper
note: a flipped payload field breaks the signed hash

name: fail-signature-tamper
note: a corrupted signature must never verify

name: fail-smuggled-member
note: a member the pack format doesn't name fails closed

name: fail-spaced-hex-proof
note: a proof node spelled with spaces between byte pairs — Python bytes.fromhex tolerates whitespace where strict hex rejects; every surface now fails closed identically

name: fail-string-leaf-index
note: leaf_index as a quoted string — JSON-typed fields must not pass through Python's permissive int() where JS === rejects

name: fail-unreferenced-junk-proof
note: a proof entry referencing nothing and reaching nothing — every proofs entry must verify; unexplained material is a lie, not decoration

name: fail-wrong-pin
note: pinning an unrelated key must not bless the pack

name: ok-clean-bundle
note: one visit, one key, media digests all present — the baseline

name: ok-decoy-successor-order
note: a consented decoy successor listed FIRST in key_rotations.json — only the highest-sequence consented pivot (K_A->K_B) may inherit trust; a first-match-in-pool verifier would pick the attacker and fail this pack

name: ok-embedded-monitor-trail
note: monitor_observation receipts embedded in the checkpoint doc — each verified under the issuer lineage and proven inside the signed head, so the watch trail travels with the pack

name: ok-float-leaf-index
note: leaf_index spelled 5.0 — JSON keeps no int/float distinction, so Number.isInteger parity means every verifier accepts integral floats identically

name: ok-float-tree-size
note: a properly SIGNED head claiming tree_size 5.0 — the signature verifies on the literal bytes, and Number.isInteger parity means integral floats verify identically everywhere

name: ok-forged-cosig-ignored
note: a cosig attesting a DIFFERENT head (or one whose signature fails after the edit) counts as absent — the pack still verifies on its own proofs; auxiliary attestations report honestly, never gate

name: ok-grafted-revocation
note: a self-signed key_revocation grafted into key_rotations.json is inert twice over — it can't join the signed trust walk, and foreign-signed receipts owe no log proof so the graft can't kill the pack either

name: ok-legacy-no-manifest
note: a pre-pin pack still verifies — the manifest is optional when absent, mandatory when present

name: ok-redacted-media
note: media bytes withheld by redaction; signed digests still verify

name: ok-revoked-case
note: revocation annotates: records + the pivot receipt itself sit in the suspect window

name: ok-rotated-case
note: case pack spanning a signed rotation — predecessor pin verifies both eras

name: ok-witness-anchored
note: the witness's attestation is itself committed to the witness's own transparency log — the pack proves the cosignature was published, not just signed and handed over

name: ok-witness-cosigned
note: an independent witness's counter-signature rides the checkpoint doc — verified under its own key, reported as an auxiliary attestation, never a gate
